teamcraft.gui.help.candidates: 1. Select candidate players individually, or use Select All Online.
teamcraft.gui.help.command.build:
Purpose: Create and assign teams from the current candidates and saved settings.
Parameters: None; candidates must exist and no TeamCraft teams may already be active.
Example: /teamcraft build-teams
teamcraft.gui.help.command.build_colors:
Purpose: Create teams immediately with a one-time color list without changing the saved colors.
Parameters: <colors...> are color IDs in team order; a short list repeats.
Example: /teamcraft build-teams colors red blue
teamcraft.gui.help.command.build_names:
Purpose: Create teams immediately with one-time names without changing the saved names.
Parameters: <names...> are names in team order; quote names containing spaces.
Example: /teamcraft build-teams names "Red Team" "Blue Team"
teamcraft.gui.help.command.clear:
Purpose: Disband every team created by TeamCraft and release its players.
Parameters: None; the candidate list and split settings are kept.
Example: /teamcraft clear
teamcraft.gui.help.command.config_colors:
Purpose: Save the color cycle used by the next split.
Parameters: <colors...> are Minecraft color IDs such as red, dark_blue and light_purple; they are used in team order and repeat when needed.
Example: /teamcraft config colors red blue green

Purpose: Clear the custom color list and restore the default 16-color palette.
Parameters: None.
Example: /teamcraft config colors reset
teamcraft.gui.help.command.config_friend:
Purpose: Set whether teammates in subsequently created teams may damage each other.
Parameters: <true|false>; true allows it and false prevents it; existing teams are unchanged.
Example: /teamcraft config friendlyfire false
teamcraft.gui.help.command.config_mode:
Purpose: Set how candidate players are ordered for assignment.
Parameters: <fixed|random>; fixed follows the candidate list, while random shuffles it first.
Example: /teamcraft config mode random
teamcraft.gui.help.command.config_names:
Purpose: Save display names in team order.
Parameters: <names...> are one or more names; quote names containing spaces, and missing names are generated from team colors.
Example: /teamcraft config names "Red Team" "Blue Team"
teamcraft.gui.help.command.config_names_:
Purpose: Clear custom team names and restore automatic color-based names.
Parameters: None.
Example: /teamcraft config names reset
teamcraft.gui.help.command.config_player:
Purpose: Switch to the players-per-team rule, which calculates the team count from the candidates.
Parameters: <players> is an integer from 1 to 1000 and is the maximum size of each team.
Example: /teamcraft config players-per-team 4
teamcraft.gui.help.command.config_reset:
Purpose: Restore only the split settings to their defaults.
Parameters: None; candidates are not cleared and existing teams are not disbanded.
Example: /teamcraft config reset
teamcraft.gui.help.command.config_team_c:
Purpose: Switch to a fixed team count and distribute candidates as evenly as possible.
Parameters: <teams> is an integer from 1 to 100 and cannot exceed the candidate count when building.
Example: /teamcraft config team-count 3
teamcraft.gui.help.command.help:
Purpose: Show the TeamCraft command summary in chat.
Parameters: None; /teamcraft and /teamcraft help are equivalent.
Example: /teamcraft help
teamcraft.gui.help.command.init:
Purpose: Replace the entire candidate list with the selected players.
Parameters: <players> selects one or more online players by name or selector, such as @a or @p.
Example: /teamcraft init @a
teamcraft.gui.help.command.init_add:
Purpose: Add the selected players to the candidate list; duplicates are skipped.
Parameters: <players> selects one or more online players by name or selector.
Example: /teamcraft init add Steve Alex
teamcraft.gui.help.command.init_clear:
Purpose: Empty the candidate player list.
Parameters: None; split settings and already-created teams are unchanged.
Example: /teamcraft init clear
teamcraft.gui.help.command.init_list:
Purpose: Show the current candidate count and names in chat.
Parameters: None.
Example: /teamcraft init list
teamcraft.gui.help.command.init_remove:
Purpose: Remove the selected players from the candidate list.
Parameters: <players> selects one or more online players by name or selector.
Example: /teamcraft init remove Steve
teamcraft.gui.help.command.intro: Every command is listed below. <argument> is required, <A|B> means choose one, and ... means multiple values are accepted.
teamcraft.gui.help.command.reset:
Purpose: Disband all TeamCraft teams, clear the candidates and restore every default setting.
Parameters: None; this is a full reset.
Example: /teamcraft reset
teamcraft.gui.help.command.status:
Purpose: Show the candidates, split rule, mode, friendly fire, colors, names and created teams.
Parameters: None.
Example: /teamcraft status
teamcraft.gui.help.command.team_color:
Purpose: Change the color and player-name prefix color of an existing TeamCraft team.
Parameters: <team> is the internal scoreboard ID, such as teamcraft_1; <color> is a color ID.
Example: /teamcraft team-manage teamcraft_1 color blue
teamcraft.gui.help.command.team_friendly:
Purpose: Immediately change friendly fire for an existing team.
Parameters: <team> is the internal ID; <true|false> allows or prevents teammate damage.
Example: /teamcraft team-manage teamcraft_1 friendlyfire false
teamcraft.gui.help.command.team_info:
Purpose: Show a team's internal ID, display name, color, friendly fire and members.
Parameters: <team> is the internal scoreboard ID of a TeamCraft team.
Example: /teamcraft team-manage teamcraft_1 info
teamcraft.gui.help.command.team_name:
Purpose: Change an existing team's display name and update its player prefix.
Parameters: <team> is the internal ID; <name> is the new name and must be quoted when it contains spaces.
Example: /teamcraft team-manage teamcraft_1 name "Builders"
